Comments: On 08/01/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Neel 1 well site following a routine complete inspection conducted on 06/20/2024 (Inspection Report 3783313).The following was observed:Emergency response plan and site information at the site entrance (Photo 1).It is recommended to install the sock at the stream crossing correctly (Photo 2). The stream crossing was in generally good condition. The sock within the channel was overwhelmed with sediment and I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 3).The sock that was at the top of the site was not installed correctly. I recommend that the sock is installed correctly and makes contact with the ground throughout the entire section. I also recommend that the sock runs parallel to the contour (Photos 4-6).The well was drilled and a well tag was posted on the fence surrounding the well (Photos 7, 8).The pit was filled and vegetation was establishing on the slopes. Open soils were noted at the top of the slope and did not have stabilization. I recommend stabilizing this area (Photos 9, 10).Due to the lack of sock maintenance and permanent stabilization, violations of 78.53, 102.22(a), and 102.4(b)1 are being issued.

Review found that Annual Production reports have been submitted and are now current. Review found that Mechanical Integrity Assessment reports have been submitted and are now current. Violations of 78a91(a) and OGA3220(A) remain outstanding. Review of annual production reports found that zero production has been reported for 12+ consecutive months and the well is still considered to be abandoned. Operator's 8/3/2021 response indicates "If the well is not capable to produce it will be added to the list of wells that require plugging per the Consent Assessment order". As of 5/24/2022: Site ID sign in place. Well ID tag was affixed to wellhead. Two production units/separators on location. One produced fluids tank installed within an earthen dike. No excessive corrosion issues found with installed equipment.

Comments: On 4/09/2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection of Diversified's Clemmer 6 plugged well site located in Springhill Township, Westmoreland County.According to Department records, this well was plugged on 4/16/2025. Therefore the well site restoration was due by 1/16/2026. A Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) was due by 3/17/2026. A Well Site Extension Request submitted by the operator on 12/19/2025 was returned by the Department (IR 4125309). No WSRR has been received to-date from the operator for this site. A COA was entered into between the Department and Diversified on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the Well Site in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216.The following was observed during the inspection:The former site access road is entirely unvegetated and appears to be used to access an active construction zone for a residential home. The plugged well site has not yet achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage. No evidence of accelerated erosion and sedimentation was observed on site during this inspection. However, no temporary Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls were observed on site during this inspection. The mailbox containing the site E and S/Restoration plans was not found during this inspection. A metal pole appears to be marking the approximate coordinate location of the plugged well. No surface fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the approximate location of the plugged well.Based on observations from this inspection, the well site and access road are not restored. The Department recommended in IR 4125309 that the Operator fully restore the well site and access road or submit a signed and completed Post-Plugging Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration. However, no Post-Plugging WSRR or Post-Plugging Landowner Waiver has been received from the operator. Therefore, a violation shall be issued in IR 4176643 for failure to restore the well site 9 months post-plugging, in accordance with the 3/07/2019 CO and A. Violations shall be issued in this inspection for failure to have the site E and S/Restoration plan available and for failure to install temporary Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls on site.

Comments: On November 26 2024, the Department conducted a routine partial inspection of the Mamont 16 Well Pad (ESCGP-3 issued on 11/30/2021 and expires on 11/29/2026) in regards to a referral from Environmental Protection Specialist (EPS) Zane Shaffer regarding an apparent spill observed outside of secondary containment. Present during today's inspection is Zane Shaffer (DEP) and Justin Ruth (CNX). The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared to be stabilized. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. The Act 9 sign was present at the time of the inspection, and appeared to be in good condition. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, site plans, and Safety Data Sheets (SDS), were present in the onsite mailbox.At the time of the inspection the operator was currently drilling the K well. Mr. Ruth stated the spill outside of secondary containment occurred because an empty barrel of AES WA II (SDS located in the onsite mailbox) was placed inside containment with the valve open therefore residual fluid in the barrel leaked into secondary containment. Then, pipes were accidentally placed on the side of the secondary containment causing a low spot/pinch point to form where the residual fluid mixed with rainwater was able to spill outside of the secondary containment. Mr. Ruth then stated that the pipes were removed off of the containment to stop the spill and all excess water/fluid in containment had been suctioned out.The Department then inspected the area of the apparent spill outside of secondary containment. Upon inspection, a spill was not active, however Zane Shaffer provided a picture of when the spill was active (photo 1). Upon further inspection of the spill, the Department observed orange fluid outside/underneath the secondary containment in the location where the spill had occurred. Conductivity readings were taking in the gravel/soil outside the secondary containment where the spill had occurred and obtained readings of 0.17mS and 0.13mS. A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.14mS.Mr. Ruth stated that they planned to remove the matting and containment and excavate all contaminated gravel/soil and reinstall the containment once complete. He stated they hoped to have all work finished by with in a day or 2. The Department requests clarification on how much fluid was spilled/released outside of the secondary containment with in 2 days of receiving this inspection report.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed spill outside of secondary containment. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending operator response.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-02-18 to Rockdale Marcellus Llc in Liberty Twp, Tioga county. 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect  brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Rockdale Marcellus Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-02-18
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 877467
Permit API: 117-21999
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-02-18
Comments: An inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of a spill of produced water to the pad surface from a cam lock fitting between a produced water tank and a battery of frac tanks. The operator estimated the volume of the spill at 15 gallons. I met with Jen Compton of Rockdale upon arriving on location. She showed me the area where the spill occurred and impacted the pad surface. She stated that the cam lock fitting on the northern-most produced water tank was found leaking on the morning of 2/17/20. She said that the produced water flowed south toward the other produced water tank. She said that some excavation was already performed but the area in front of the south produced water tank is continuously collecting fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (EC). She said that it appeared that fluid is flowing out from underneath the south produced water tank and flowing into the area in front of the tank. A vaccuum truck was present on location during this inspection and was sucking up the fluid as it seeped into the area in front of the south tank. Ms. Compton also said that there was a truck driver on location one hour before the leak was discovered which leads them to believe that the fitting leaked for 1 hour at most. I took several EC readings in front of the south produced water tank where fluid was pooling. Every EC reading was greater than 19.99 mS/cm. No other substantial volume of water was present in the area near the produced water tanks. When I looked beneath the south tank, the gravel appeared to be saturated with fluid. It appeared that the fluid pooling in front of the tank was coming from beneath the south produced water tank. The areas Ms. Compton said had already been excavated were covered with approximately one half inch of snow. These areas appeared dry other than the snow. I took a sample, #0718-160, from the area in front of the south produced water tank which were sent to the state laboratory the same day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Li, and Al. The Department requests a justification for the reported spill volume. The Department recommends moving the south produced water tank to assess the soil beneath it and vacuum the fluid there as needed. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation due to the surface area of the pad which appears to have been impacted. Violations noted.

Comments At time of inspection, well appears plugged with an erected monument. According to records, drilling occurred 8/16/2006-8/18/2006. During this inspection, the Department was unable to locate an on-site E&S plan. The Department’s regulations provide that the E&S plan shall be present at the project site during all stages of an earth disturbance activity. Contractor currently on-site re-grading location. There do not appear to be any installed temporary E&S BMPs during this inspection. The Department’s regulations provide that a person conducting an earth disturbance activity shall design, implement, and maintain E&S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Department observed accelerated erosion and sedimentation occurring as a result of an unstable access road. Sediment was observed tracked onto the adjoining road (Luciusboro Road) from the access road. Sediment-laden water was also observed traveling off the access road onto Luciusboro Road and into a roadside ditch. Violations are being issued for failure to have an E&S plan on-site for all stages of an earth disturbance activity and for failure to design, implement, and maintain E&S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Following this inspection, the Department called Operator representative Mark Gawel and left a message. At 1520, Mr. Gawel returned the Department’s phone call. Mr. Gawel stated that he is currently at the location removing the tracked sediment off of Luciusboro Road. The Department recommended that the Operator implement measures to control and/or prevent the sediment laden water from entering the roadside ditch from the access road. Mr. Gawel agreed to address this concern. The Department stated that the E&S plan was unable to located while on-site. Per Mr. Gawel, the E&S plan should have been on-site with the contractor. The Department recommended that the Operator post E&S plans in a manner that allow the Department to locate them. The Department asked what E&S BMPs were identified in the E&S plan. Mr. Gawel stated that he would have to verify before answering.

Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/06/2025
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8232621
Permit API: 021-21034
Unconventional: No
County: Cambria
Municipality: Susquehanna Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/06/2025
Comments: On May 6, 2025, an inspection was conducted in response to a spill at the A J Stahura 8 well site in Susquehanna Township, Cambria County. This spill was discovered by the operator on the day prior to this inspection, which is suspected by the operator to have been caused by trespassing vandals opening the brine tank valve when operator representatives were not present onsite. The Department spoke with operator representative Will Warfel on 5/05/2025, who stated that the last time operator representatives were onsite was most likely one month prior to detecting this spill, when the chart was changed and the brine tank level was read. Reporting of this spill is covered in IR 3974873. Mr. Warfel was onsite was onsite with the Department during this inspection.The following was observed:Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Mr. Warfel who identified a stream crossing of Kings Run as part of the access road to the well site (see photo 1). He then requested recommendations for dispersing the weight of commercial vehicles that haul the excavation equipment onsite to protect the cross-culverts when they traverse this location (see photo 4). Further review will be conducted by the Department regarding this matter. What appears to be scouring was observed on the upstream side of the stream crossing. A brown foam that appears to be biological in nature was observed at the top of the water in this location (see photo 3). An erosion channel was going down the access road toward the downstream location of the stream crossing (see photos 5 and 6). Mr. Warfel stated that this access road is utilized by additional parties. Further review via Google Earth Historic Imagery suggests that this portion of the access road most likely predates the well site. Additional muddy tire rutting was observed in the rest of the access road going toward the well site (see photos 7 and 8).The well head is equipped with a well tag and appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photo 10). The operator's information is posted on the brine tank (see photo 11). The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photos 12 and 14). The brine tank valve appears to have been closed, therefore it appears that the release has been ceased (see photo 13). Plastic sheeting was placed on the impacted area within the earthen berm. Distressed vegetation was observed where brine fluids were reported by the operator to have traveled downslope (see photos 15-17). Elevated conductivity was detected in the ground starting approximately 25 feet downslope of the brine tank (see photos 18-25). Mr. Warfel confirmed during this inspection that the operator will conduct remediation in accordance with the requirements of Act 2, and that remediation will start on the day of this inspection with light excavation.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued from this inspection for releasing production fluids to the surface of the ground. The operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 business days of the spill or release. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, the regulation substance involved, where the spill or release occur, the environmental media affected, any impacts to water supplies, buildings, or utilities, and interim actions planned, initiated, or completed.Any new impacts discovered or identified during interim remedial actions or site characterization should also be reported to the Department within 15 calendar days of discovery.Within 180 days of the spill or release the operator must perform a site characterization to determine the extent and magnitude of the contamination and submit the site characterization report to the undersigned.The operator shall assess impacts to waters of the Commonwealth from the spill or release.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/13/2025
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8224739
Permit API: 125-29141
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Donegal Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/13/2025
Comments: On 03/13/2025 an Incident Response inspection was conducted at the DMC Well Site in response to an operator reported release.On 03/13/2025 Range Resources Representative, Dennis Furmanek, reported an approximately 84-gallon release of frack fluid off containment at the DMC Well pad located in Donegal Township, Washington County.Range Resources representative, Matthew Dorsey, was on site at the time of inspection. Mr. Dorsey informed the Department that the release was discovered today (03/13/2025) at approximately 5:00 am, that the quantity released was approximately 84 gallons, and that some of the fluid had since been removed via vacuum truck. The source of release was determined to be a hole in the manifold of a blender, located on the southwestern side of the well pad. The release occurred from the damaged blender, filled and overtopped the primary containment, filled and overtopped the secondary containment, and was release onto the pad aggregate. Mr. Dorsey stated that the cleanup will commence after the frac is completed and equipment is removed in approximately 8 days.Range Resources representative, Dennis Furmanek, contacted via phone call to provide updates. Mr. Furmanek stated that a large sump will be dug behind the spill site on the southwestern end of the well pad to collect any remaining fluids and remediation will begin next week after tear down is complete. He stated that he would notify the Department when the cleanup will begin.Mr. Furmanek also stated that he believed the elevated readings that were obtained from the driving lane on the eastern side of the pad and near the site entrance were caused from road salt that had been tracked onto the site from the large number of sand trucks. He stated that the area in which the elevated readings were observed was the same area in which the sand trucks consistently traveled and parked. He also stated the area had recently been sprayed with water to reduce the dust, which would explain the mud observed in those areas that were exhibiting elevated conductivity.Conductivity probe calibrated on 03/13/2025.The following was observed during the inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance. Various co-operations were taking place at the time of inspection and frac equipment was observed on site (Photos 1-2).-Large amounts of pooled fluid and mud were observed on a driving lane near the site entrance on the eastern side of the well pad. Elevated field conductivity readings of 3.37 ms/cm and 4.43 ms/cm were observed (Photos 3-8).-The mixer where the release originated, the secondary containments, and the surrounding areas were observed. The extent of impact could not be determined because much of the impacted area was located beneath the secondary containment. A small sump and hose were observed, located in the impacted area beneath the white plastic sheeting covering the temporary waterline. Field conductivity screening was conducted throughout the impacted area. Elevated field screening values ranged between 4.29 ms/cm and greater than 20 ms/cm. The discharge onto the ground and failure to dispose of fluids, specifically produced fluid, are violations of 78a.54, 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act (SWMA) 301. The potential to have indirectly impacted Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC) is a violation of 91.34(a) (Photos 4-16).-Pooled fluid was observed in tire tracks near the site entrance. Field conductivity screening was conducted throughout the area. Elevated field screening values of 2.48 ms/cm and 2.93 ms/cm were observed. Non-elevated field conductivity screening values of 78.5 s/cm and 1,189 s/cm were observed on either side of the temporary water line (Photos 17-20).Determination:Violations issued.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARD OPR LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 08/28/2020

Violation ID: 893201
Permit API: 027-21534
Unconventional: Yes
County: Centre
Municipality: Snow Shoe Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 08/31/2020
Comments: Follow-up site inspection on August 31, 2020 at ARD's COP Tract 231 well pad. Prior to my site inspection I spoke with Rick Hall of ARD via phone. The contractor discovered during excavation a small hole in the buried 2" steel line, which was the result of the undetermined amount of fluids released on August 28, 2020. According to Mr. Hall, approximately 50 tons of impacted gravel/soil were removed during excavation on August 28, 2020. Impacted gravel/soils were placed on secondary containment stationed onsite and the materials were covered. Impacted gravel/soils were observed during my inspection. Water was observed on the secondary containment with field screenings ranging from 52.8 uS/cm- 65.1 uS/cm. The Department recommends removing the rain water from the secondary containment.After excavation and repairing a section of the 2" dump line, the operator opted to leave the trench open and staked off with orange safety fence. According to Mr. Hall, there are three pipe lines running in the same ditch line. The first is the 2" steel dump line located at approximately 2' 8" deep below the surface. A 3" steel discharge line located in the same ditch line and a 6" steel suction line located approximately 4 feet away from the 2" dump line and is approximately 5' 8" below the surface. Mr. Hall stated that a bed of sand is located beneath the 6" suction line and conductivity readings were elevated in sections of that sand. Tuscarora Geological & Environmental Services collected samples from the impacted sand area. Mr. Hall requested that the sample results be expedited. Samples results are pending.While I was onsite I viewed the open trench. I screened throughout the 2" dump line side of the trench and readings ranged from 0.100 mS/cm to 0.300 mS/cm. I screened on the 6" suction line side of the trench and I was getting elevated readings >4.00 mS/cm in an approximate 2' diameter area. These elevated readings were adjacent to where the 2" dump line was repaired. As I moved away from that 2' diameter area, screenings dropped to 0.100 mS/cm to 0.400 mS/cm.No new violations have been cited. Outstanding violations remain.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-09-17 to Cabot Oil & Gas Corp in Auburn Twp, Susquehanna county. properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Cabot Oil & Gas Corp
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-09-17
Violation Code: OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
Violation ID: 863496
Permit API: 115-22557
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Auburn Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-09-17
Comments: The Department was on-site in response to the report of a spill incident of more than (5) gallons of diesel based drilling mud that occurred on 9/16/19 at 17:05 hours. The weather conditions are sunny skies with a light breeze, and temperatures in the upper 60's. Remediation of the impacted area affiliated with the spill was in progress. Resource Environmental of Montrose, PA is the Cabot subcontractor delineating the extent of the impact via the use of a photoionization detector (PID) meter to determine the presence of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds. H&P Flex Rig 259 is the drilling rig on the location. The current drilling depth of the M Powers 12H well is (4,351.59) feet. Cassidy Moyer, DEP WQS and I initially met with Mike Stansfield, Drilling Engineer of Cabot in the site office/company man trailer. Mr. Stansfield provided the following information relevant to site activities and the spill incident. "The rig is on the M Powers 12H well. Remediation of this well is in progress. The 4H and 8H wells will be drilled to total depth (TD). All other wells on the pad have been drilled to TD. A low cement top was found when a cement bond log was run. Perforations were shot in the production casing at (4,430) and (6,000) feet. Cement was pumped into the production casing and through the cement retainer. The cement retainer didn't hold in the production casing. The cement retainer was drilled out. Diesel based drilling mud overflowed the 12H well casing vent tank onto containment. Some of the mud got outside the containment. The mud came out of the top of the tank in the form of a flow, then rolled off the containment to the pad surface, and then it flowed under the containment. The spill volume is over (5) gallons, but may be under (42). We may be able to calculate the volume of the spill, and determine it is under (42) gallons. The spill happened around 5 PM yesterday. Marlon Droddy, the site company man found the spill and reported it to Mike Cromley, the site safety man. Remediation of the impacted area started last night. Initially, we were not able to dig under the vent lines. We eventually moved the vent tanks and the containment to evaluate the extent of the impact.” Resource Environmental provided the following information relevant to remediation of the impacted area. “We arrived here today at 9AM. A small excavation of the impacted area was done yesterday. The excavation is now at (5) feet below the ground surface of the pad. Three test pits have been dug to determine the extent of the impact. The test pits were excavated and backfilled North, South, and just next to the impacted area. The test pits were excavated to a depth of (5) feet. Visually impacted material was not observed in the test pits. The PID meter didn't detect any readings in the test pits. Initial PID reading of soil in the impacted area was (592) parts per million (PPM). The PID reading in the vent tank was (741) PPM. We use (25) PPM as a standard threshold. In addition to using a PID meter to guide the remediation, we will use visual and olfactory senses.” Steve Catalfamo of Cabot indicated impacted material will most likely be transported for disposal to Alliance Landfill in Taylor, PA, and Cabot will attempt to determine the volume of the spill. The Department left the site at 14:20.

Including the current Safety Data Sheet (SDS) required under law to be present at the well site, the location of the SDSs at the well site, the name of the position in the operator’s organization responsible for providing the information in sub clauses (I) and (II).
Violation ID: 8232158
Permit API: 125-28458
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Smith Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/01/2025
Comments: On May 1, 2025, an inspection was conducted in response to a spill at the Malinky well pad in Smith Township, Washington County. According to the incident report that was submitted by Range Resources representative Nate Smiell, approximately 200 gallons of diethylene glycol was released to the surface of the well pad on the day of this inspection at 11:27 AM. No waterways are reported to have been impacted and remediation crew is on the way for cleanup. This spill report was submitted to the Department on the day of this inspection at 12:45 PM. Mr. Smiell was present onsite for this inspection. Additional representatives from Range Resources and SPSI were also onsite conducting remediation.Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Mr. Smiell who further explained that diethylene glycol was being pumped from the GPU units in preparation for installation of secondary containment, per the requirements of an active Consent Order and Agreement (CO and A) between the operator and the Department, when the pump truck operator erroneously pumped the diethylene glycol from the GPU into a chamber of the truck tank that was already full. This resulted in an estimated 200 gallons of diethylene glycol being released from a vent on the top of the truck's vessel and to the surface of well pad. Three spill cleanup drums were filled with absorbent material that soaked up the standing ethylene glycol on the well pad surface. Two rolloff boxes are expected to be required to contain the impacted material. Mr. Smiell then confirmed that the operator will conduct remediation in accordance with the requirements of Act 2. Mr. Smiell reported that at the time of this inspection, the majority of the impacted material appears to have been removed. This is based on testing that was conducted by Mr. Smiell throughout the impacted area, utilizing a glycol test kit, however a third-party environmental consultant is scheduled to take confirmation samples on the day following this inspection, per the requirements of Act 2. Excavation and remediation of the impacted area remains ongoing at the time of inspection (see photos 4-8, 12, and 17-19). The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Some minor potholes were observed in the access road (see photo 2). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is onsite (see photo 3). No Safety Data Sheet (SDS) was located onsite for diethylene glycol, the pollutant released during this incident. The GPU units are in the process of being equipped with secondary containment (see photo 9). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 10). Well 2H is equipped with a well tag with no staining or evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it, and it appears to be in production (see photos 14 and 15). Six additional wells are onsite that appear to be in production (see photo 13).Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued from this inspection for releasing pollutants to the surface of the ground and for failure to keep the SDS onsite for the pollutant released.

Violation ID: 901084
Permit API: 081-21338
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/02/2020
Comments: On December 2, 2020, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at Seneca Resources Gamble Pad K. No E&S issues were observed during the time of inspection. The site is stable and well vegetated meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. There are a total of 10 wells capable of producing located on this well pad. All wells are tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. There are 8 GPUs, 2 line heaters, and 3 steel vertical production fluids tanks onsite. Both GPUs, line heaters, and production fluid tanks were stationed in secondary containment. The DEP observed a Seneca Resources contractor pumping water from a well cellar and actively discharging the water off the the pad edge. The contractor provided the log sheet from today's field tests of pH and conductivity of the well cellar. The contractor stated that one well cellar is recorded on the log sheet due to the contractor logging only the highest conductivity of the 10 well cellars tested. The contractor stated that they had pumped out 7 of the well cellars prior to DEP arrival. The well cellar water was being discharged off the North pad edge. Well cellar water that was discharged had only travelled about 15 ft. downslope off the pad edge. There was no estimate of the amount of water pumped out of the 7 other well cellars prior to the DEP arrival.The discharge of water from a well cellar off the well pad is a violation of Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 91.34(a).

Comments: Onsite for a routine inspection. The well is equipped with a pump jack, rods, and tubing. The pump jack does not have a motor/engine or belt to operate the well. The surface casing is vented and the well is labeled with a metal sign near the well. Tank Battery: It was noted in the previous site inspection, Inspection Report # 3198057 dated 5/26/2021; that one of the 210bbl steel tanks were showing signs of corrosion and weeping fluid. The steel tank has been replaced with a 100bbl poly tank. The old steel tank remains onsite along the access road/well site. The poly tank is full with brine water and the bulkheads are leaking fluid to the earthen dike. The area around the tank is wet. The dike drain is open and continuously discharging (dripping) fluid to the ground. There is a visual impact area downslope of the open dike drain. The impact area extends 40-50' from the drain pipe. Fluid from the dripping drain pipe was collected and field tested. The field screening indicates that the fluid is brine water with conductivity readings of 4,470 uS. The discharge of brine to the ground is an unlawful act. The Department requests that the operator make repairs to the tank and remediate the impacted area according to state regulations and policies for spills/releases on oil and gas well sites. Violation(s) are cited.

Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow-up to the 7/11/22 inspection in which fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (EC) was found near the freshwater tank. I first inspected Pad B. New containment liner has been put down for the upright produced water tanks, where fluid with elevated EC was found during the 7/11/22 inspection. A new offloading area for trucks has been constructed adjacent to the produced water tanks as well. Fluid on this section of secondary containment had an EC of 6.91 mS/cm. I recommended to Mr. Hamill that this fluid get vacuumed up and he said that he would have someone do that immediately. Puddles of fluid were present on the pad surface beneath the mechanics trailers near the freshwater tank and the secondary containment for the upright produced water tanks. These puddles had an EC of between 1.7 to 3.14 mS/cm. I recommended to Mr. Hamill that these puddles be vacuumed up as well. The area of the pad along the east pad edge, where fluid with elevated EC was found during the 7/11/22 inspection, was dry. On Pad A, the wells are in production. A battery of frac tanks is present within secondary containment. Equipment is staged on pad A for the frac on Pad B. No issues noted.Violations remain outstanding from 6/24/22 for the release of an unknown volume of produced fluid on Pad B.

Inspection Date: 8/20/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a release of at least 5 gallons of a mixture of produced fluid and stormwater was discovered on the well pad following a re-frac on the 5H well. The notification also stated that a contractor, Tobias, would excavate the impacted pad material. I met with company man Levi Lee upon arriving on location. He showed me the location of the release. It rained steadily during this inspection. Tobias had already scraped a thin layer of gravel off of the top of the impacted area at the time of inspection. Mr. Lee said that Creston Environmental was also present to take samples and characterize the release. Some areas of the impacted pad area were more damp than others. No standing fluid was observed in this area of the well pad. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the pad material according to the Hanna soil conductivity meter ranged from 0.41 mS/cm to 2.86 mS/cm. The higher EC readings were found closer to the well heads and the lower readings were taken farther away from the well heads toward the southeast pad edge. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Violations noted.Violations remain outstanding for the release from June 1, 2026. These violations will be closed upon demonstration of Act 2 remediation standards.

Report Details
Inspection Client: APOLLO RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/25/2024
Violation Code: OGA3220(A) - PLUGGING REQUIREMENTS - Failure to plug the well upon abandoning it.

Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Fairfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/25/2024
Comments: On 11/25/24 an On Site FUI was conducted by the DEP to determine if the operator had addressed the violations cite on ID# 3661814 and #3791669. - Well/Operator ID posted on location. - Onsite equipment consists of wellhead, meter, electric service connection box, and three produced fluids tanks. Tanks appeared sound. - Much of the wellhead and flow lines were wrapped with insulating material. Electric service box appears to have been damaged and inoperable. - A review of Annual Production Reports found that production for 2022 and 2023 were zero with a comment of "well temporarily not producing. Due to the well reported as zero production for 12+ consecutive months the well is considered abandoned in accordance with the regulations. Violations of section 78.91(a) and section 3220(a) will be continued. - A review of Mechanical Integrity Assessment reports found that MIA report has been submitted for 2023.
